note: Every external source this project knows about. Nothing outside this file may be linked to or ingested. `use` is the whole point: link_only sources are NEVER read for content by any code path (there is no fetching code in src/reference at all, and a test enforces that); data sources may have a CSV placed under data/reference/datasets/ with its own manifest. Licences were checked on the date shown and are not guaranteed to have stayed put — run `python scripts/check_links.py --verify` to re-check the URLs, and re-read the licence page before relying on any of them.

sources.name: Khan Academy
sources.notice: All Khan Academy content is available for free at www.khanacademy.org
sources.why_link_only: ShareAlike, not NonCommercial, is the blocker: text pulled into a generated note would push CC BY-NC-SA onto the note. Linking and embedding are explicitly permitted with attribution plus the notice above.

sources.name: CORE Econ — The Economy 2.0
sources.notice: CORE Econ material is free to read at core-econ.org
sources.why_link_only: NoDerivatives. The most open-looking teaching content in economics still forbids distributing modified material, so summarising it into a note is out. Reading and linking are fine. Undergraduate level — use it for depth, not for AS scope.

sources.name: ZNotes
sources.why_link_only: Per-reader watermarked PDFs ('authorised for personal use only by ... at ...') and all rights reserved. Read them; never ingest them.

sources.name: Economics Help
sources.why_link_only: Individually authored UK site, all rights reserved. Strong on UK macro worked examples.

sources.notice: Source: World Bank Open Data, CC BY 4.0

sources.name: UK Office for National Statistics
sources.notice: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0

sources.name: Our World in Data
sources.notice: Source: Our World in Data, CC BY 4.0. Underlying data may carry its own terms — check the chart's source line.

sources.name: OECD Data Explorer
sources.caution: CC BY 4.0 applies to OECD content published from 1 July 2024. Earlier material sits under the older OECD terms — similar in effect, but record it as 'OECD Terms' in the dataset manifest, not as CC BY.

sources.name: International Monetary Fund
sources.notice: Source: International Monetary Fund. Used under the IMF Terms of Use.
sources.caution: NOT Creative Commons. The IMF's own terms permit copying, derivative works and redistribution with attribution, subject to an integrity condition and carve-outs for third-party material inside IMF publications. Never record this as a CC licence.

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India
sources.caution: Read the copyright page before using anything beyond headline statistics. Included because local context makes a stimulus land better for a student in India.
